External_shared_identifiers_schema_json_.description: Opaque stable resource identifier. Prefixes are descriptive, not authorization claims.
Monotonic decimal revision represented as a string.
Logical capability resource pool identifier. Pools may span multiple host nodes.

External_capacity_manifest_schema_json_u.description: Total combined physical memory charged against a unified-memory HostNode parent budget to prevent double-counting host and device memory.

output_watermark.description:
Null for text-only stages. Otherwise its sample_rate_hz must equal
the response-level sample_rate_hz and its generated_pcm_samples must
not exceed hard_output_ceiling_samples when that ceiling is set.

External_internal_execution_control_open.description:
Authoritative execution state on the gateway. `submitting` and `unknown_quarantined`
continue to hold reserved capacity until stop evidence is confirmed.

Monotonic high-water summary over the authoritative interval ledger.
`generated_pcm_samples` and `sample_rate_hz` are authoritative; audio
milliseconds are derived only for reporting as
`floor(generated_pcm_samples * 1000 / sample_rate_hz)` and are not a
stored or independently mutable meter. When
`hard_output_ceiling_samples` is non-null it must be greater than or
equal to `generated_pcm_samples`.

Closed execution-state to cleanup-state matrix. Active states still own
capacity. A successful execution has completed cleanup. A failed
execution may clean up without a dispatched request (`not_required`) or
only after verified termination (`complete`); an unknown execution must
use `unknown_quarantined` together with quarantined cleanup.

Terminal status must expose evidence consistent with its result.
A successful execution has an engine terminal response and no error. A
failed execution must carry a stable error code and either have no
dispatched request or verified termination evidence.

A failed execution may use `cleanup_state=not_required` only when no
request reached the engine. `engine_request_id` and `dispatched_at` are
therefore required and null for that branch; omitting either would make
dispatch history ambiguous and could release capacity while an engine
request is still active.

Submission is persisted before an engine request. Active execution,
and successful completion require an observed dispatch time. `submitting`
and a failure that never dispatched require
it to be null. An unknown quarantined execution may have an ambiguous
dispatch outcome and keeps capacity quarantined either way. An abort with
no observed dispatch time is allowed only with verified whole-instance
termination evidence; recovery must not invent a dispatch time.

idempotent_replay.description:
Present only on POST. True when the response is the stored result
of an identical earlier intent with the same `intent_id`.

created_at.description: Time the intent identity was first recorded; immutable across replay.

External_shared_runtime_states_schema_js.description: Controller observation. `absent` means no matching instance generation was observed.

External_internal_runtime_control_openap.description:
Peak reservation must be greater than or equal to steady reservation in
every memory counter used by the selected architecture. Producer
validation rejects a smaller peak because cold-load headroom cannot be
released before steady state is reached.

External_shared_capability_domains_schem.description: Unified memory shares one physical host/device pool; discrete memory accounts host RAM and device VRAM separately.

RuntimePendingSnapshot.description: Coordinator has durably recorded this immutable request but has no controller observation. A null runtime never proves absent, ready, stopped, or resource release. Timestamps belong to the coordinator record, not the controller response.

expected_head_version.description: Null means the initial head must be absent; first creation is serialized by host and unique instance identity. A revision requires that exact existing head.

staging_result.description: Trusted producer only. Register once while executing and eligible. Preserve expected_version CAS: after a lost response query the original identity; an exact receipt replay at the current version is read-only even after later stop. Mismatches conflict. Does not publish or change terminal/stop/budget facts.

audio_staging_result.description: Trusted producer only. The audio receipt is a separate optional property so the JSON receipt above keeps its exact shape; send at most one of the two, never both. The same registration, expected_version CAS, original-identity replay and no terminal/stop/budget effect apply, and the receipt must match the original output stream and cover every generated sample.

External_internal_execution_control_open.description:
Private immutable receipt from the trusted execution adapter after complete
version-pinned readback. Not a publication, execution terminal or release fact.
Initial supported container is Transcription JSON; TTS media is not enabled here.

Trusted private version-pinned audio receipt. The producer verifies the
encoded payload and its source PCM clock. Registration requires the original
output stream, sample rate and authoritative generated_pcm_samples to match
audio.source_pcm_samples, with real recorded output intervals and the frozen
ceiling respected. Generated intervals for this file execution must cover
[0, source_pcm_samples) without gaps, not just reach its max-end watermark.
Registration never appends samples or proves stopping.
PCM delivery length is source_pcm_samples * 2; WAV contains that PCM; MP3
uses the source clock rather than decoder padding. At most 64 MiB delivery.
Old ledger readers must be upgraded before any audio producer is enabled.

Source mono PCM16LE clock, before delivery encoding; not MP3 decoded-frame
length (which may include codec padding). duration_ms is exactly
floor(source_pcm_samples * 1000 / sample_rate_hz).
Initial persistent file-TTS scope is 24 kHz mono, at most 64 MiB source PCM.

redact_execution_command.description: Trusted deletion coordinator permit only; verify the authoritative deletion job/dependency scope before calling. Clear private command content only after execution cleanup and lease release. Preserve identities, request/command digests, fencing, stop facts and an immutable deletion tombstone. Replays use deletion_job_id and evidence digest; never authorize re-execution.

enforced_at.description: Time of this successful enforcement confirmation. Replay may refresh inventory and this time while preserving the same durable minimum and proof.

External_internal_execution_control_open.description:
The execution gateway derives the private staging namespace from
`workspace_id` and `submit_intent_id`. command contains the complete frozen
input and effective parameters. command_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785
canonical command JSON; mismatch is invalid_execution_request. Same intent
with a different canonical command is submit_intent_conflict. Callers cannot supply an output object
key, path prefix, bucket, or external URL. Input storage references must
identify immutable owned assets and match the command workspace.

max_output_audio_ms.description:
Hard output-audio ceiling for stages that synthesize audio. Use
null for ASR, alignment, and other stages that cannot emit audio.
The referenced manifest stage must declare `emits_audio_pcm=true`
for a non-null value. The gateway stores
`hard_output_ceiling_samples` as
`floor(max_output_audio_ms * sample_rate_hz / 1000)`. A manifest
stage that emits audio PCM rejects a null value.

sample_rate_hz.description:
PCM sample rate used for output metering. Required and non-null
exactly when `max_output_audio_ms` is non-null; null for text-only
stages.

VerifiedStopEvidence.description: Verified termination of this submitted execution and release of its incremental resources. This does not imply that the shared engine process exited; instance baseline release requires the separate RuntimeStopEvidence contract.
